size_and_complexity:
The code is too large and too intricate for the assurance it currently achieves:
- It is about 8,400 lines: C 7,506 plus M 896, each exactly at its D2a cap.
- The fold has hundreds of guard sites, 915 mutated guard ids, a 572-test suite that takes about an hour, and 35 equivalence arguments.
- In spite of that, this review found 1 critical and 9 majors. Several sit in paths added or rewritten for v2.1: the CLEAR/T23 interplay, the MK-1 assemble rewrite, the setup-loop handback and the A-series inbox handling.
- Each fix round has added code and test machinery faster than it has removed risk.

The operator surface is small and well disciplined: go, found, answer, a bootstrap block, and a printed DO: line to follow. The counts are honest, and one run walks through in about 22 helper commands and 60 Drive calls.

The burden on an LLM operator is not small:
- A 38-case, two-reader qualification needs about 3,600 or more tool calls over several days.
- It is run inside a single coordinating turn that may not end while anything is open.
- It needs the owner's 'continue' after any turn end.
- It relies on exact retyping of attested values, a mailbox protocol that contradicts the README, and a Drive tool with approval refusals.

The Dot can follow it for one run. Executing it for 72 runs is not shown. That can only be shown on the operator VM (G-4), and only after the disk-growth, NO_CONVERSATION and handback defects are fixed.

- Add explicit pause points so the procedure fits the platform rather than the reverse.

rationale:
Under the gate rules any CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE critical blocks admission. INT-R3-01 is a CONFIRMED critical. It was reproduced twice with the real fold and plan, the runner's REFUSED record entries were checked in cps_job.py, and I re-read the cause at fold.py:103-108 and :315 and plan.py:42-46. A refused runner command on an interrupt or freeze resolution chain followed by the documented CLEAR leaves a run that can never freeze. Qualification then cannot reach FINAL, and no kit change can repair it mid-run. In addition, CONFIRMED majors fall on integrity rules:
- INT-R3-02: the O58/O46 outcome, or a forced fabricated attestation.
- M-1: the audit skips the kit-in-force checks on the path to scoring.

Further majors make ADMIT_WITH_CONDITIONS unavailable even apart from the critical: R3-EQG-01, SAF-1/OPX-R3-02, SAF-2, SAF-3, M-2, OPX-R3-03 and the PLAUSIBLE OPX-R3-04.

The reproduction itself is clean, and v2.1 closes review 2's findings with real mechanisms:
- every claimed count reproduces exactly at tree 4f996ef9 and helper sha 55a09073;
- the runner is untouched;
- all 35 survivors are equivalent on reachable chains, and only two record corrections are needed.

The candidate therefore fails on new defects, mostly in v2.1's own additions, not on a failed reproduction. A narrow v2.2 that fixes the listed items, adds a killing test for each, and passes a full G-1 again is the right path. - **One critical consequence, rare trigger.** After a T23 RUNNER_REFUSED halt on an interrupt or freeze chain, a CLEAR leaves the run with nothing pending. findings.title: A cleared RUNNER_REFUSED halt (T23) on an interrupt or freeze chain loses the pending resolution, so the run can never freeze and the qualification can never reach FINAL
findings.where: deploy/vm2/cpsvm2/core/fold.py _update line 315 (R['snapshot'] set for every STAGE, refused ones included) and pending_resolution lines 103-108; core/plan.py pending_chain lines 42-46 and next_action row 23 line 148; cli.py carry() (a Stop UNCLASSIFIED in phase OPEN becomes commit_halt); worker.py commit_end; plan._chain_row X6
findings.evidence: Runner v4 run_stage (deploy/run/cps_job.py lines 3112-3125) appends a REFUSED entry to the run record on every preflight refusal of an existing, unfrozen job folder, so record_changed is true. chain_next then takes X6, which writes a STAGE with refused, then T23, then HALTED RUNNER_REFUSED. e23 calls _update, which moves R.snapshot.seq past the RESTORE whose resolution (INTERRUPT or FREEZE_LOST) was still pending. After the CLEAR, pending_resolution returns None: there is no ARCHIVED role, the run is not INPUTS, and current is still set. next_action therefore falls to row 23, Stop UNCLASSIFIED, and carry() commits HALT UNCLASSIFIED. I reproduced this with the fold and plan (probe probes/t23.py, built on tests/core_world). The steps were: GENESIS; prepare A/case01 (START G1); RESTORE with NOTHING_WRITTEN, which gives action INTERRUPT (rows T42, T44); interrupt REFUSED with the record changed (T23, phase HALTED, code RUNNER_REFUSED); CLEAR (T59). Output: `after CLEAR phase OPEN current A/case01 pending_chain None`, then `next_action: Stop(code='UNCLASSIFIED', handback='C')`. The variant probes/t23f.py (WRITTEN, so FREEZE_LOST; freeze REFUSED NOTHING_TO_FREEZE) gives the same result. Consumer chains are not affected, because consumed is not set on a refusal and the consumer re-runs. A fixed helper cannot rescue the series. A non-config-only kit is refused while a run is in flight (current is set): session.kit_change returns KIT_CHANGE_WITH_RUN_IN_FLIGHT and fold _s5 refuses it. accepted_helper_tree_sha256 is not a CHANGEABLE_KEY. A second Q series is refused by QUALIFICATION_SERIES_EXISTS.
findings.scenario: Qualification, reader A, case X. After a reset the Dot answers NOTHING_WRITTEN for G1, so the action is INTERRUPT. The runner's interrupt is refused in preflight, for example INTERRUPTION_TIMES from a clock edge, INTERRUPT_NOT_ALLOWED, or a check_release_static refusal; for a FREEZE_LOST resolution, a freeze refusal. It appends its REFUSED record entry. The helper commits STAGE(refused) and halts RUNNER_REFUSED. The maintainer issues a config-only clear kit. The CLEAR is committed, and the next go commits HALT UNCLASSIFIED. Every later clear or reset gives the same result. Run X/A is never frozen, final_ready is never true and FINAL is unreachable. The 38-run qualification is stranded with no mechanism to recover. The trigger, an unexpected runner refusal on these two chains, is uncommon, but the HALT/CLEAR path exists precisely for unexpected conditions, and the consequence matches the critical definition.
findings.fix_hint: Keep the pending action across a refused STAGE. For example, have pending_resolution compare against the last non-refused snapshot, or keep a separate R['resolution_done_seq'] that only a NEXT result of that chain sets. Alternatively, after a T23 on a resolution chain, route to the freeze chain (as X5 does), so that the run freezes as a failed run. Add a fold/plan test: T23 on interrupt and on freeze, then CLEAR, then next_action must be a RunChain, not Stop UNCLASSIFIED.
findings.verifier_evidence: I reproduced this with the real fold and plan in a fresh clone at bbe768f (deploy/vm2 tree 4f996ef9). Probe: verify_integrity/probes/t23.py, built on tests/core_world.World. Steps: GENESIS; _prepare A/case01 GENERATE (START G1); RESTORE with NOTHING_WRITTEN, giving rows ['T42','T44']. At that point pending_resolution is INTERRUPT and pending_chain is ('interrupt', ...). plan.chain_next('interrupt', REFUSED INTERRUPTION_TIMES, record_changed=True) gives X6 end STAGE. Committing that STAGE (refused=INTERRUPTION_TIMES) gives ['T23']: phase HALTED, halt {seq 4, RUNNER_REFUSED}. next_action then offers the CLEAR, which commits as ['T59']. Cause: fold.e23 calls _update, which sets R['snapshot'] = {'seq': this STAGE's seq} for a refused STAGE too (fold.py:315). pending_resolution (fold.py:103-108) then drops the resolution, because its seq < snap. None of the remaining branches of plan.pending_chain applies (no ARCHIVED role, status ACTIVE, no delivery), so next_action reaches row 23. cli.py:832-833 turns Stop UNCLASSIFIED in phase OPEN into commit_halt. findings.title: A cache invalidated in load_cache moves PENDING.json away without recording moved_pending, so verify_head's pending-sha FORK check and the everyday RECHECK (SD-59) are skipped for an entry that may already be uploaded
findings.where: deploy/vm2/cpsvm2/cli.py load_cache lines 132-164 (invalidate('invalid_') with st, pe, bl, wk set to None) versus do_clear lines 626-637, which passes moved=...; verify_head line 924; core/session.py _commit line 513
findings.evidence: Only do_clear builds `moved = {'seq', 'name', 'sha256', 'uploaded'}` from env.pending and passes it to new_work. load_cache's invalidation runs whenever STATE, PENDING, BLOCK or RESTORE_WORK is unreadable, a boot id differs, or halt_local is set without HALT.json. It moves the pending file into outbox/v2/invalid_*/ and starts a fresh RESTORE_WORK with moved_pending None. In everyday mode, _commit then returns DONE without the step-6 RECHECK, because the condition is `F.is_q(st) or moved_pending.uploaded`. verify_head never compares the head copy with the pending entry's sha256.
findings.scenario: Everyday series E1. A DELIVERY or STAGE entry N+1 was uploaded by the Dot, but its FIND had not yet confirmed it. A damaged cache file in the same boot (for example a killed write leaving STATE.json unreadable, or HALT.json removed by hand) invalidates the cache. The new session's head search, with Drive lag, settles on N, and the RESTORE takes seq N+1. If the late original lands only after the RESTORE is confirmed, there is no RECHECK to catch it. Two different copies of N+1 then exist, and are found only at the next head search (LINK_MISMATCH) or by the audit. This is fail-closed, but it misses a check the clear path has.
findings.fix_hint: In load_cache, when PENDING.json is readable, build the same moved_pending record as do_clear before invalidating, and pass it to new_work. Alternatively, run the RECHECK in every session after an invalidation that moved a pending.
findings.verifier_evidence: From the code: cli.py load_cache (lines 132-164) calls invalidate(env, 'invalid_'), which moves PENDING.json among the cache files, and sets st = pe = bl = wk = None. advance() then calls new_work(env) (cli.py:794) with moved_pending None. Only do_clear (cli.py:626-637) builds moved = {seq, name, sha256, uploaded}. As a result, verify_head's moved_pending FORK test (cli.py:924-926) and the everyday RECHECK condition (session.py:513) do not apply after such an invalidation. This matches the delta, which defines moved_pending only for a clear (§2.4.3 step 3, §2.4.4), so it is a design gap. Severity stays minor, and the triggers are narrower than the finding suggests. durable.write_doc writes atomically with a self_sha256, so a killed write is unlikely to leave an unreadable STATE. savepoint.finish writes STATE before it removes PENDING, so a kill between the two gives pe.seq == hs, where the entry is already confirmed. A boot-id mismatch cannot carry a PENDING across a real reset, because BASE is on the /home/agent tmpfs. The remaining trigger is an out-of-procedure removal of HALT.json while halt_local is set and a PENDING is in flight, and it matters only in an everyday series. Qualification still runs RECHECK on every restore. The audit or the next head search (LINK_MISMATCH) catches it fail-closed.

findings.title: make_kit.py assemble (MK-1, added in v2.1) refuses a legitimate kit in which 7 or more members have identical bytes, and its subset list grows exponentially
findings.where: deploy/make_kit.py:241-275 (groups are keyed by (size, sha256), so identical members at different paths fall into one group; all 2^n-1 subsets are built, then combos > 64 gives Fail)
findings.evidence: Probe: trees with n per-case files cases/c<i>/ADMISSION_NOTE.json all containing '{"admitted": true}\n'. `make_kit.py pack` then `assemble --expect <the packed kit's sha256>` on the untouched A and B parts: n=2 and n=6 were written; n=7 printed 'FAILED: path dispute: more than 64 combinations of member paths; the kit was not written'. For n identical members the code builds 2^n-1 subset lists before the 64 cap (n=25 means about 33 million lists, a memory or time blow-up on the Dot, under rebuild_kit's 3600 s timeout).
findings.scenario: A qualification or everyday kit built on the parts route ('no maintainer binary upload') that holds several identical small members, for example per-case notes, empty tables or the same text file in several case folders. Every copy arrives intact, yet v1mod.rebuild_kit stops KIT_NOT_REBUILT and the series cannot start. pack does not warn, so the maintainer learns of it only on the Dot.
findings.fix_hint: Apply the MK-1 path dispute only to paths that the copies disagree on (paths seen in only one copy, or unsafe), and accept every path that both A and B name; or refuse at pack time any kit whose identical-content groups would exceed the cap. Add a test with legitimate duplicate members.
findings.verifier_evidence: Code: make_kit.py:241-275 groups valid candidates by (size, sha256), so identical members at different paths share one group. For each group it builds all 2^n-1 subsets as options, and the product over groups raises Fail once it exceeds 64. This happens before --expect is tried, even though the first option (every path) is the right one. Reproduced on invented trees with make_kit.py pack, then assemble --expect <sha of the packed kit> on the untouched A and B parts: 6 identical NOTE.json members gave 'written t6/rebuilt.zip'; 7 gave 'FAILED: path dispute: more than 64 combinations of member paths; the kit was not written'. Also reproduced with only 4 pairs of identical small files (c1a/X.md == c1b/X.md, ... 3^4 = 81 > 64): FAILED, same message. findings.title: The mailbox protocol and README rules 1/6/8 contradict each other: who carries out a maintainer message, which conversation CLAIM.md names, and how a HANDBACK C clear reaches the Dot
findings.where: README.md lines 168-172 (rule 1), 199-204 (rule 8), 361-369 (section 6); docs/handoff/DOT_MAILBOX_PROTOCOL.md step 5 (line 14: CLAIM.md holds 'this run's conversation id'; 'carry it out exactly as written') and step 3; PROBE_RESULTS M010/M012 (a mailbox worker claimed the message); deploy/vm2/session_start.sh (takes no helper lock)
findings.evidence: Rule 1 defines the coordinating conversation as the one 'which a maintainer message's CLAIM.md names'. CLAIM.md is written by the claiming run, and in M009-M012 that run was a mailbox worker, so CLAIM.md names a worker that rule 1 forbids from running the bootstrap or any helper command. The fixed mailbox prompt (authority O62) tells that same run to 'carry it out exactly as written'. Section 6 says a HANDBACK C stop is cleared only by a maintainer message carrying the bootstrap, but rule 8 lets the owner pause the mailbox check for the whole series and gives no other channel for that message. If the check is not paused, then at 6 hours it uploads REPLY_ABANDONED_ for the series message and takes the next message, which could be a clear or a probe, in a worker. session_start.sh checks no HelperLock: it git-checks-out the commit and re-runs setup_vm_user.sh into ~/cps-tools whenever the commit changes, even while a stage runs.
findings.scenario: (a) A series starts from a maintainer message claimed by a mailbox worker. Following rule 1 literally, the Dot treats the worker as the coordinating conversation, or the worker runs the series (M008-type deaths; M010's worker had no elevated route). (b) A series stops HANDBACK C while the owner has paused the check, so the clear message never arrives and the series is stranded until the owner improvises. (c) The check is not paused, so a mailbox worker carries out a later maintainer bootstrap concurrently with a running stage and swaps the checkout and the toolchain under it.
findings.fix_hint: Resolve OQ-28 before G-4. Name the coordinating conversation by an explicit statement in the starting message rather than by CLAIM.md. Define the clear channel when the check is paused (for example, the owner pastes it into the coordinating conversation). Make session_start.sh take the helper lock, or refuse while FOREGROUND.json names a live stage of this boot.
findings.verifier_evidence: Text contradiction, confirmed. README rule 1 (line ~168) defines the coordinating conversation as the one 'which a maintainer message's CLAIM.md names'. DOT_MAILBOX_PROTOCOL.md step 5 has the claiming scheduled run write CLAIM.md with 'this run's conversation id' and then 'carry it out exactly as written'. So CLAIM.md names the mailbox-check run, which rule 1 says 'never runs the bootstrap or a helper command'. README §6 says a HANDBACK C clear arrives only as a maintainer message, and rule 8 allows the check to be paused for the whole series without naming another channel. session_start.sh, read in full, takes no HelperLock and checks no FOREGROUND.json. It rewrites vm.sh and HINT.json and, when the boot/commit marker differs, re-runs setup_vm_user.sh into TOOLS. Mitigations: rule 8 (MAILBOX_UNSETTLED) stops a series that does not settle the mailbox, and the 6-hour/pause question is the open owner item OQ-28 (delta 2455, 3225). The CLAIM.md naming contradiction and the missing clear channel are not covered there. Scenario (c) needs a different commit to re-run setup, so it is less likely. The consequences (a series run in a worker, as in M008-type deaths, or a stranded clear) are plausible but cannot be reproduced off-platform. I kept major for the documented contradiction on the series-start path.

findings.title: A series requires one unbroken coordinating turn of thousands of tool calls, and there is no exit from waiting on an AI-role conversation or an over-long command
findings.where: README.md lines 174-180 (rule 3), 215-216 (OPEN_CONVERSATION and CONTINUE_CONVERSATION: check every 5 minutes, no limit), 72-75 (poll until exit), 396-401 (about 3,600 tool calls); deploy/vm2/cpsvm2/vio/v1reuse.py:905 (runner subprocess timeout 7,200 s; the printed max= is not enforced)
findings.evidence: Rule 3 forbids ending the turn, setting a wait or setting a wake-up while a command runs or an S, G or V conversation is open. Every non-STOP block leads straight to the next action, so there is no safe pause point. After any turn end the Dot only resumes when the owner replies 'continue', because the mailbox check does nothing while a claim is younger than 6 hours. README section 7 puts a qualification at about 3,600 tool calls (counting each 5-minute check as one call, while each check is a sleep 300 call plus a read-back), plus conversation time, stage time and restores: several days. The probes show at most an 1,800 s command and one wait/wake (M008, M010), never a turn of this length. No README line says how long to keep checking a conversation that has not ended (for example, one blocked on a platform approval prompt, which M006 says some actions need every time), or a command that runs past its printed max (up to 7,200 s).
findings.scenario: In a G conversation, a tool call waits for an owner approval prompt. The Dot checks every 5 minutes indefinitely, may not end its turn and has no rule to END_CONVERSATION or notify the owner. Alternatively, the platform ends the long turn (context or time limit): the series stops silently until the owner notices and types 'continue', and lost context drops the notes (the refused uploads and the started_utc reading).
findings.fix_hint: Define pause points where the Dot may end its turn: after a confirmed FROZEN entry, or after any confirmed SAVE when no conversation is open. Give explicit limits: tell the owner, through NOTIFY or the paused line, after N minutes of an AI conversation without an end and after max+X seconds of a command, and set when to END_CONVERSATION with UNSURE. Make G-4 measure the turn length and the context behaviour.
findings.verifier_evidence: The text is confirmed. README rule 3 (lines ~174-180) forbids ending the turn or setting a wait while a command runs or an S, G or V conversation is open, and the OPEN_CONVERSATION and CONTINUE_CONVERSATION rows say only 'check it once every 5 minutes', with no limit and no escalation. Only the turn-end line 'CPS paused ... reply continue' exists. The printed max= is not enforced: cli.py run_stage prints max but sets no alarm (grep for signal.alarm, setitimer or RLIMIT finds nothing), and v1reuse.py:905 runs the runner with timeout=7200. README §7 estimates about 3,600 tool calls for a qualification. Whether a coordinating turn can actually last that long, and whether a G conversation can block indefinitely on an approval prompt, are platform behaviours this harness cannot reproduce (G-4 measures part of it). It is a realistic gap in the operator procedure: no defined exit or owner notice on an unbounded wait.

findings.title: README section 7 understates PNG parts, polls and wall time, and compares restores measured on different journal lengths

findings.title: Refused or uncertain upload notes are never retired by the helper's confirmation, which loops WAIT_APPROVAL until the owner uses the exact words
findings.where: README.md lines 224-225, 244-258 (rules 3, 4 and 7)

A timed-out upload never had a platform prompt to approve, and a file later re-uploaded and confirmed by the helper is never dropped from the notes. Every later session asks approval=, the Dot must answer pending, and the helper stops WAIT_APPROVAL HANDBACK A.
findings.scenario: A timed-out upload is later confirmed. After the next reset, every session start stops at WAIT_APPROVAL until the owner explicitly says 'denied' about a file that is already on Drive.
findings.fix_hint: Let the Dot drop a note once a later SAVE of that name is confirmed, or have the helper print the names it confirmed so the Dot can retire them.
findings.verifier_evidence: README §3 rows UPLOAD_REFUSED and WAIT_APPROVAL, and §3.1 rules 3, 4 and 7 (lines ~224-258), keep a refused or uncertain upload in the notes until the owner says 'approved or denied'. 'If the owner only says to continue, keep it'. A later helper-confirmed save of that name is not a reason to drop it. A timed-out upload counts as refused. findings.title: Audit never re-checks entries against the kit in force: an unaccepted helper tree and GENESIS gates that differ from the kit pass clean
findings.where: deploy/vm2/cpsvm2/maint/audit.py:245 (E.validate_entry(doc) with no cfg); audit.py:270-276 (the kit is used only for release and jobs); spec §3.4 (helper.tree_sha256 'must be in config accepted_helper_tree_sha256'); core/fold.py:584-588 and 640-653 (genesis gates drive forced_for and the w_abs double-absence window); outcome.py:75 (p3 tolerance sets the O52 windows)
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with the test_maint Journal harness (exp/e1.py and exp/e4.py in my scratch folder).
(1) Seq 3 written with helper.tree_sha256 = 'ab'*64, which is not in the kit's accepted_helper_tree_sha256 [CW.TREE]. Result: 'e1_helper_tree rc 0 clean True anoms []'.
(2) The genesis kit's config gates say p1_transcript_export='no' and p3_clock_tolerance_seconds=0, but the GENESIS body gates say 'yes' and the World's values. Result: 'audit rc 0 clean True []'.
The VM checks these only through the helper itself (validate_entry with cfg; GATES_CHANGED against state.genesis.gates). The maintainer side never ties GENESIS to its kit, so a journal with self-consistent gates is folded under whatever gates it carries. HELPER_VERSION is the same string 'cps-vm-helper.v2.1' for every v2.1 build (746ea98, 2cfaac5, 1802e06, local patches). AUDIT.json also never reports the genesis release_sha256, kit_sha256 or helper tree, and score_check takes no expected value.
findings.scenario: The Dot runs a qualification series with an older or locally patched v2.1 tree, or with a kit whose gates were edited. Example: p2_lag_seconds lowered, so w_abs falls to 60 s and a rebase that supersedes an AI START needs much less evidence of absence. Example: p1_end_after_reset changed, which changes forced_for. The audit re-folds the journal under the gates the journal itself carries and reports CLEAN. score_check builds a plan and scoring proceeds on a series the admitted helper and the kit never authorized.

findings.where: deploy/vm2/cpsvm2/cli.py:669-670 (go_checks pending branch) with cli.py:740-748 (do_found persist, then handback emit without DOWNLOAD lines) and vio/savepoint.py:250 (on_found sets loop['verify'] before handback)
findings.evidence: on_found puts the found part's unknown copies into loop['verify'] and also returns ('handback', refused_name). do_found persists PENDING with verify non-empty and prints only STOP UPLOAD_REFUSED HANDBACK A, with expect {'command': 'go', 'kind': 'pending'} and no DOWNLOAD line. On the next `go`, the basis is current and env.pending['verify'] is non-empty, so loop_verify runs on_verify on files the Dot was never told to download. The result is slip(DOWNLOAD_MISSING), loop['slips'] += 1, and a REFUSED line with exit 4. Reproduction: scripts/scen.py pending_two_parts, World D1 with the ALLFZ01 part refused on first upload. Output: '[found] 3 ... DO: STOP UPLOAD_REFUSED HANDBACK A name=CPSJ_D1_000014_ALLFZ01.json', then '[go] 4 ... REFUSED DOWNLOAD_MISSING CPSJ_D1_000014_LEDGER01.jsonl', followed by FIND lines for both parts. The FakeDot oracle treats this as an unexpected refusal and stops.
findings.scenario: A FINAL (LEDGER+ALLFZ), DELIVERY (DELIV+DLOG) or PNG commit uploads several parts. One upload is refused by the approval review and another part lands. The owner approves, and the Dot runs `go`. It gets 'REFUSED DOWNLOAD_MISSING <the other part>' even though it never got a DOWNLOAD line for that part. One of the three slip asks (SLIP_ASKS=3) is used up, so later real download slips reach the sticky SLIP_LIMIT (HANDBACK C) one ask sooner. The README text for DOWNLOAD_MISSING ('a DOWNLOAD file is missing') misleads the operator. No evidence is lost, and the loop recovers through the re-FIND.
findings.fix_hint: After a handback, either print the DOWNLOAD lines for loop['verify'] before the STOP, or record in the handback expect that no download was asked, and have go_checks skip loop_verify for it (the block() call will then print the DOWNLOAD block). Add a world test with two parts, one refused.
findings.verifier_evidence: Code: savepoint.on_found (savepoint.py:223-252) sets loop['verify'] for the found part's unknown copies and also returns ('handback', name). do_found persists PENDING, then emits only the STOP block with no DOWNLOAD lines and expect kind 'pending'. On the next `go`, go_checks (cli.py:669-670) runs loop_verify; on_verify reports the never-requested file as DOWNLOAD_MISSING, and slip() increments loop['slips']. Reproduced with my own probe (World D1, drive.refuse={'CPSJ_D1_000014_ALLFZ01.json': (1,)}, default FakeDot approve=True): `found` exit 3 `STOP UPLOAD_REFUSED HANDBACK A name=CPSJ_D1_000014_ALLFZ01.json`, with no DOWNLOAD line printed before it. The next `go` gave exit 4 `REFUSED DOWNLOAD_MISSING CPSJ_D1_000014_LEDGER01.jsonl`, then FIND lines for both parts. PENDING.json showed slips=1 and verify=[], and FakeDot recorded it as an unexpected refusal and stopped. The loop recovers through the re-FIND and no evidence is lost. Slips are per commit, and reaching SLIP_LIMIT would need several such coincidences in one commit, so minor is right.
